The proposed answer, G(g, g+b) = g + 2b − 2, appears correct.

**Lower bound.** Normalize the ruler to [0, D] and let S be the set of integers in [0, D] missing from it, so |S| = D + 1 − n. Each missing integer destroys at most 2 of the D unit-distance pairs (y, y+1). The number of unit differences is therefore at least D − 2(D + 1 − n), and it must be at most g. This gives D ≥ 2n − g − 2 = g + 2b − 2, and the argument is sound.

**Upper bound.** I did not verify the construction in full. It removes b − 1 points from [0, g + 2b − 2], which requires the removed set to realize each distance d at most d − 1 times, with the end effects accounted for. The stated threshold g ≥ (7/4)(b^{3/2} − b) + 1 is what makes this possible. As a spot check, I verified b = 2 (remove one interior point from [0, g+2]) and the b = 3, g = 5 example. Both satisfy the g-fold condition with diameter g + 2b − 2.

The result also matches the known theorem I recall for this threshold, G(g, g+b) = g + 2b − 2.
